title: PR drafting selects deterministic titles and changelog entries across AzureRM surface combinations

provenance.originSummary: Synthetic benchmark matrix for the initial PR drafting surface-classification contract.
provenance.whyItMattered: The prompt must choose one stable title while keeping mandatory companion surfaces visible in changelog decisions.
provenance.genericCondition: Multiple sanitized runs cover new and existing Terraform surfaces plus documentation and contributor-guidance classifications.

description: A scenario matrix covering new Resource, Data Source, List Resource, enhancement, bug-fix, documentation-only, and contributor-guidance-only title precedence.

scope.notes: The fixture defines separate synthetic runs; the listed paths are the union of their modeled scopes.

mustCatch.description: A new Resource plus required List Resource uses the new Resource title while retaining separate feature changelog lines.

The description retains every proven user-facing discriminator guard, meaningful computed output, list scope, and state-normalization behavior once instead of replacing them with supporting implementation details.

When an update actively clears multiple independently configured values that the API would otherwise retain, the description names every retained-value family without narrating serialization or polling mechanics.
The evidence plan reads compact clear-path logic in a changed custom request marshaller that owns omit-versus-clear behavior, while keeping marshalling mechanics subordinate in the draft.
The description strictly outlines changed behavior without correctness judgments, defect findings, missing-test speculation, recommendations, or field-by-field CRUD narration.
A new Resource and Data Source sharing one Terraform name use the exact combined title shape.
New Resource, Data Source, and List Resource entries use their exact automation-ready surface forms even when they share one Terraform name.
Registration, Resource Identity, SDK shim, and polling companions do not receive independent changelog entries without distinct user-facing impact.
A title driven by new surfaces retains distinct enhancement entries for changed existing Resources and Data Sources in the same coherent service-package change.
Existing Resource and Data Source behavior receives separate owner-specific changelog lines even when both surface kinds share one Terraform name.
List Resource support added to an existing Resource uses the New List Resource title.
Existing Resource bug fixes and enhancements use concrete surface-first title wording with bug-fix precedence when both apply.
A proven correction to premature lifecycle success on an existing Resource renders as a BUG line and checks Bug Fix, while implementation-only polling remains subordinate.
A new object flowing through an existing consumer's unchanged schema and ID association path is not presented as a newly enabled compatibility enhancement.
An importer-only ownership guard is described as preventing import or adoption and is not generalized into rejecting the object across all Resource lifecycle operations.
Compact prose keeps one sibling Resource's create retry separate from another sibling's readiness and terminal-state waiting instead of assigning every behavior to both surfaces.
Each material lifecycle behavior is represented by its owner, exact operation paths, behavior kind, and observable outcome before prose or changelog compression.
A retry proven only for Resource A's create path is not transferred to Resource B or widened to update and delete when those paths only add waiting behavior.
Existing Resource and Data Source changelog owner tokens use exact undecorated automation-ready formatting with only Terraform names in code spans.
Documentation-only and contributor-guidance-only runs use Docs and Contributing title forms respectively.

mustNotFlag.description: A required companion List Resource must not displace or expand the new Resource title.
The AzureRM draft must not use this toolkit repository's bracketed title prefixes.
The combined title must preserve the literal `(Data Source|Resource)` text instead of rewriting it as a natural-language conjunction.
Supporting-only polling or plumbing work must not be promoted to an independent changelog entry.
Client wiring, registration, helper reuse, generated code, or vendoring must not displace proven material user-facing behavior in the description.
Drafting must not report defects, grade correctness, identify missing work, recommend fixes, or narrate implementation exhaustively.
Resource and Data Source behavior that shares one Terraform name must not be combined under one surface identifier.
The draft must not claim that an existing consumer newly supports the new object type when no changed enabling implementation proves that behavior.
